implications.says: the cart passed out by the town gate, and the berths lie inside the quay gate: it was not going to a vessel
it went up Mill Lane, where Mr. Garrick writes that the casks had been going to his cellar: it took them there
the first pass was signed at Saltmere while Mr. Pell was in London: he did not sign it
one hand signed all three, and it was not Mr. Pell's
J.P. on a pass of the Custom House that is not Josiah Pell's is Jonas Prout's
the casks left the bond store on passes the clerk signed
and they went to a cellar in the town, not aboard a ship: Mr. Prout let the brandy out of bond
